page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server utilizing the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor on the x86_64 architecture, running at 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.0 GB of RAM per core. Graphics and parallel processing are driven by two NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace family, delivering a combined 96 GB of VRAM. This configuration does not include local storage.

Benchmark data places this server in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance under stress-ng, as well as Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations. The AMD EPYC processor achieves top-tier results in bzip3 decompression, Geekbench image and text processing, and Passmark database operations. Memory performance is more varied; while cached read-only memory bandwidth is strong (top 25%), the Passmark memory score falls into the average category (middle 50%). For LLM inference, the dual L40S GPUs achieve top-tier prompt processing and text generation speeds with small 135M models, strong performance with medium 7B models, and average performance with large 70B models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density by pairing a 32-core AMD EPYC CPU with 384 GB of RAM and dual enterprise-grade GPUs, though the lack of local storage requires external storage solutions. This hardware profile is suited for workloads such as machine learning inference on small to medium models, data processing, parallelized scientific simulations, and GPU-accelerated rendering tasks.
